surprises.description: The preview expected AllianceBernstein’s adjusted revenue and EPU (about $885M and $0.85), but the call reports Indian cement sales and volumes in rupees and tonnes. These are not comparable results, so the preview provides no usable baseline for most of the reported figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 21% YoY to INR 3,561 crores” and H1 grey cement volumes rose to “11.3 million tonnes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. net revenues” of “~$885M” and “Adj. diluted EPU” of “~$0.85.”

surprises.description: Despite 21% H1 sales growth and 19.38% volume growth, H1 EBITDA grew only 2%, while Q2 EBITDA fell sequentially. The preview’s AB earnings estimates do not anticipate this cement cost-versus-realization pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Despite strong volumes, H1 EBITDA grew only 2% to INR 1,138 crores as cost increases outpaced realizations,” and “Q2 EBITDA [fell] to INR 500 crores from INR 639 crores in the prior quarter.”

surprises.description: Management expects fuel costs to rise further, adding roughly INR 80–100 per tonne in both Q3 and Q4, with the full impact in Q4. The preview instead discusses AB’s fees, AUM, and expenses and contains no expectation of this cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fuel cost is “expected to climb toward INR 2.00,” with a power-and-fuel cost impact of “roughly INR 80-100 per tonne in both Q3 and Q4, with the full impact in Q4.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed guidance of 23 million tonnes-plus but would not commit to 24 million tonnes, which some investors expected. The preview contains no cement-volume guidance or discussion of these operating risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed FY26 grey cement volume guidance of 23 million tonnes-plus,” while “declining to commit to the 24 million tonnes some investors expect.”

surprises.description: Net debt increased, and management now expects it to peak near INR 6,000 crores, with net debt/EBITDA reaching 2.25–2.35 around end-FY27. The preview does not discuss this company’s debt or expansion-related leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose to INR 4,571 crores (from INR 3,370 crores)” and is expected “to peak near INR 6,000 crores”; net debt/EBITDA is “projected to peak at 2.25-2.35 around end-FY27.”

surprises.description: The call lays out substantial expansion spending—INR 3,500 crores this fiscal and roughly INR 2,500 crores annually thereafter—toward 50-million-tonne capacity by FY30. This capital plan is absent from the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capex is INR 3,500 crores in the current fiscal” and is expected to run at “roughly INR 2,500 crores annually thereafter toward the 50-million-tonne capacity target by FY30.”

surprises.description: The call reports a nascent paint business with Q2 revenue of INR 115 crores and a small EBITDA loss, while retaining FY27 revenue guidance and expecting positive full-year EBITDA. The preview has no paint-business expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Paint generated “INR 115 crores revenue in Q2” with “a small Q2 EBITDA loss of INR 2 crores”; management maintained FY27 revenue guidance of “INR 500-550 crores” and expects “full-year positive EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Cement prices had risen, but management still sees a further INR 10–15 per-bag increase as necessary to offset costs and says it may only be achievable after Diwali. The preview does not address cement pricing or this remaining cost-recovery gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: Prices rose “about INR 20 per bag from mid-September to mid-October,” but a “further INR 10-15 per bag hike is still needed to offset cost pressures, likely only achievable after Diwali.”

surprises.description: The call provides commissioning targets for the Jaisalmer and Bikaner facilities, a later target for the Mahan coal block, and rising quarterly incentives—operating details not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Jaisalmer and Bikaner are “on track for first-half FY28 commissioning”; Mahan is targeted for “H1 FY29” at “about INR 1.25 per unit”; quarterly incentives of “INR 45 crores are expected to exceed INR 50 crores.”
